title: A monic rational divisor of a monic integer polynomial is integral
statement: Let $F\in\mathbf Z[T]$ be monic and $G\in\mathbf Q[T]$ monic [def-weil-polynomial-ring] such that $G$ divides the image of $F$ in $\mathbf Q[T]$ [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map]. Then $G$ has integer coefficients: $G$ is the image of a (monic) polynomial in $\mathbf Z[T]$. (Gauss's lemma, in the form: $\mathbf Z$ is integrally closed in $\mathbf Q$, and the coefficients of a monic factor of a monic integer polynomial are integral over $\mathbf Z$, being polynomials in its roots.)
